snippet.text: Solution: a lens level's `probe` makes it run as two conversations. Each role reads wording of its lens's own, from a table in core that names the `trust-boundary`, `tests` and `correctness` lenses. A repository's lens of another name reads the wording of the built-in its `extends` chain reaches, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-16, so `trust-boundary-probes` with `extends: trust-boundary` probes in trust-boundary's words. A level that sets `probe` is refused when it loads in two cases. One is a lens whose chain reaches no built-in with wording. The other takes a built-in's name without extending it. [The per-lens wording decision](decisions/2026-11-16-probing-wording-per-lens.md) records why. The planner, on the level's tier, reads the change, the decisions at base and the findings of the change's last earlier revision, and records a numbered attack plan, each attack with its reason and what a passing and a failing probe would print. The prober, on `probe.prober`'s tier or the level's, receives that plan alone and answers every attack with a probe through `run_probe` that shows something, or a skip with its reason. A probe runs the head's own code at every step of an attack's route that the sandbox can run, and stands in only for what cannot exist there, such as a CI runner, an upload service or a real login; its output and the finding say which steps were stood in for, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-16, which [the stand-in decision](decisions/2026-11-16-probes-stand-in-only-for-infrastructure.md) records. A probe that timed out, was cut, was ended by a signal, ended with no record of how, or exited 125 to say it could not test, shows nothing and answers no attack. An attack whose probe failed is answered only by a finding resting on that failed probe, never by a plain skip, and a finding the verifier later refutes still answers it, as [the decision of 2026-11-17](decisions/2026-11-17-a-failed-probe-needs-a-finding.md) records. trigger.snippet: Solution: a lens level's `probe` makes it run as two conversations. Each role reads wording of its lens's own, from a table in core that names the `trust-boundary`, `tests` and `correctness` lenses. A repository's lens of another name reads the wording of the built-in its `extends` chain reaches, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-16, so `trust-boundary-probes` with `extends: trust-boundary` probes in trust-boundary's words. A level that sets `probe` is refused when it loads in two cases. One is a lens whose chain reaches no built-in with wording. The other takes a built-in's name without extending it. [The per-lens wording decision](decisions/2026-11-16-probing-wording-per-lens.md) records why. The planner, on the level's tier, reads the change, the decisions at base and the findings of the change's last earlier revision, and records a numbered attack plan, each attack with its reason and what a passing and a failing probe would print. The prober, on `probe.prober`'s tier or the level's, receives that plan alone and answers every attack with a probe through `run_probe` that shows something, or a skip with its reason. A probe runs the head's own code at every step of an attack's route that the sandbox can run, and stands in only for what cannot exist there, such as a CI runner, an upload service or a real login; its output and the finding say which steps were stood in for, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-16, which [the stand-in decision](decisions/2026-11-16-probes-stand-in-only-for-infrastructure.md) records. A probe that timed out, was cut, was ended by a signal, ended with no record of how, or exited 125 to say it could not test, shows nothing and answers no attack. An attack whose probe failed is answered only by a finding resting on that failed probe, never by a plain skip, and a finding the verifier later refutes still answers it, as [the decision of 2026-11-17](decisions/2026-11-17-a-failed-probe-needs-a-finding.md) records. A probe that failed only because the prober wrote it wrongly is closed instead: `skip_attack` names it and says why it never exercised the attack, and the lens's record shows that reason. An attack every failed probe of which is closed is answered, as [the decision of 2026-11-18](decisions/2026-11-18-a-wrongly-written-probe-is-closed-with-a-reason.md) records. An attack still unanswered after one reminder ends the lens, as [the decision of 2026-11-16](decisions/2026-11-16-an-attack-needs-a-probe-that-shows-something.md) records. A finding names a probe that failed. Two attacks that fail on one defect report one finding, which answers both and rests on the probe that first showed it; [issue #545](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/545) would keep every probe it rests on. The review runs each probe a claim cites again before its verifier starts, once a probe, in a durable task a concurrent review attaches to, as [the probe-reruns decision](decisions/2026-11-12-probe-reruns.md) records. A finished probing run is reused when its request is unchanged, as any lens run is, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-16 that [the decision of 2026-11-16](decisions/2026-11-16-finished-probing-runs-are-reused.md) records: a repeat review attaches to it or copies it, with its probe evidence and the reruns stored for it, and runs no probe. Its request holds its whole probing environment, the host's sandbox release included, so a review under another writer, grant, time limit or host probes again. A lens task with a level that probes starts no verification wave. The verifier receives the plan, the probe and both runs, and cannot confirm a claim whose probe did not fail again. A candidate's evidence fits 128 KiB: past that, Melian cuts the longest parts a model or the head wrote, keeping both ends of each and the row of the attack the probe answered, and tells the verifier what it cut and that a cut is never grounds to refute. Evidence that does not fit even with every part cut asks no verifier, and the review reads not reviewed. The stored records stay whole, as [the evidence-budget decision](decisions/2026-11-16-probe-evidence-bounded.md) records. The level's token and tool budgets and each probe's time limit bound the probes, below fixed limits no level can lift. Those are 48 probes a run, and 64 MiB of git's listing of the head, as [the fixed-limits decision](decisions/2026-11-09-probing-fixed-limits.md) records. Telemetry shows the budgets, the probes and their time. No shipped level probes yet. By the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-07, the built-in `trust-boundary` lens's `deep` level turns probing on once the live measurement picks the planner and prober routes. Until then a level that probes is one a repository or an eval's own lens declares, extending a built-in the table names. A level that probes reports nothing it finds by reading: its planner reports only an injection attempt, and its prober only a finding a failing probe backs. [Issue #497](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/497) lets it read too. Until then Melian's own rounds run two lenses, by the maintainer's rulings of 2026-11-16. `trust-boundary` reads, unchanged. `trust-boundary-probes` extends it, probes at `deep`, and is held there by a floor in `melian.yaml`. Its planner runs on the level's `heavy` tier and its prober on `medium`, a pair no measurement picked, as [the decision](decisions/2026-11-16-probing-on-for-melians-own-rounds.md) records. Where a probe may not run, the level runs as it would without `probe`, and its record says why. That holds for a fork's head, under `trust.writers: false`, on a host where the sandbox cannot run, and for a head whose own tree refuses probes, past its limits or with a link out of it. The review tries the head's tree before it chooses to probe, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-13. [The decision](decisions/2026-11-07-trust-boundary-level-that-probes.md) records the rulings and what it gives up. `melian review --require-probes` fails such a level instead, and fails one whose prober asked for a probe that could not run, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-16. It also fails a level whose every probe for an attack showed nothing, under [the ruling on issue #493](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/493#issuecomment-6905471494). Each failure names one of nine causes, which `--probe-gaps <file>` writes as JSON. The `melian round` workflow reviews that way, after a step that proves on the runner that a probe reaches none of the round's secrets, as [the round's probing decision](decisions/2026-11-16-round-job-probes-behind-containment.md) records.

The preference file's path in the standards' source, which names the host. Who set the route, and the credential, by [the run identity decision](../decisions/2026-11-08-lens-run-identity.md). The key holds the run under the fixed nonce, its route, thinking, level, budgets, instructions and prompt with the enclosing functions, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-14; the injection policy and the name of the section Pi renders it in; the installed versions of Pi Durable and pi-ai, which render the system prompt and turns and write them into each provider's request, read from each package's own `package.json`; every tool offered by name, description, schema, output limits and argument bound, and the bounds every lens tool cuts what it shows to, `lensToolLimits`; both failover wordings, `handoverWording`, the one that continues earlier work and the one that starts afresh, since a conversation's history picks between them at run time; a probing run's tools; base, head, `escalateAt` and the escalation; and the standards by text, source and trust. A lens with `standards: false` keys no standards text, only their source and trust, so turning a lens's standards off asks its runs again once, by [the decision of 2026-11-19](../decisions/2026-11-19-lenses-get-only-the-standards-they-cite.md). As a lens record's key, it lets `melian records relay` take a lens run's early copy, with no check, beside a round that reads a lens record under the same key, by [issue #397](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/397). For a run that probes, it holds the probing wording its planner and prober read: the shared lines, and the entries in core's `lensProbingWording` of its lens's `probesAs`, or of its own name. So a change to one lens's words asks no other lens's run again. [Issue #493](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/493) changed the trust-boundary lens's probing wording on purpose, so its probing runs are asked again once. For a run that escalates to another, it holds the shared lines, which carry its findings on, by rule 8 and [the per-lens wording decision](../decisions/2026-11-16-probing-wording-per-lens.md). For a run offered `list_mutants`, the key holds the instrumenter that answers it, `@stryker-mutator/instrumenter`, by [the decision of 2026-11-16](../decisions/2026-11-16-lens-request-keys-the-mutant-instrumenter.md). It holds its version, read from the `package.json` of the package the tool resolves. It holds its source, the checkout's install or Melian's, or `unavailable` when neither resolves. A run not offered the tool keys nothing more. A probing run's environment names its host by one value, `probingHost`, whose architecture and Node version come from core's `hostFacts`: the sandbox's platform and kind, the installed sandbox-runtime release, read from its own `package.json`, and the CPU architecture and version of the Node that runs the probe. Left out of that value: the operating system's release, since the platform names the system; the CPU's model, since the architecture names the instruction set Node runs; whether the filesystem folds case, since a probing run is reused only from its own checkout's store, so a temporary directory moved to a volume that folds differently copies a run probed under the other rule; and the host's locale and clock, which no probe should hang on. Left out of the request, by [the probing reuse decision](../decisions/2026-11-16-finished-probing-runs-are-reused.md): what Melian's probe runner gives a probe and what `run_probe` returns, until [issue #437](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/437), so a release that changes them copies a run probed under the old code; and what the read paths hold, the installed dependencies of the code under test among them, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-16, so a reinstall between two reviews of one head copies the run and its conclusive reruns. A task stored before the key, lens task version 6, holds no request key, so nothing is copied from it and the first review after the upgrade runs every lens once. The lens tools' own code, `list_mutants`'s included, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-15: the text each tool returns to the model, what each tool does, and the lens extension's code, which the key cannot hold as data. Rule 8 forbids hashing source at run time, so [issue #437](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/437) ties a code version to a hash of them in a test; until then a change there reuses runs asked under the old code. Chord, Pi's composition runtime, which shows a model nothing. The packages Pi Durable and pi-ai depend on, such as the AWS and Smithy packages under pi-ai's Bedrock client, by the maintainer's acceptance of 2026-11-15: they resolve through caret ranges, so a reinstall can change how a request is built while both versions stay the same, and hashing the install would ask every lens again whenever any dependency moved; [issue #470](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/470) keys only the packages that build a model request. The packages beneath the instrumenter, such as Babel, which a reinstall can move while the instrumenter's version stays the same, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-16, [as recorded on pull request #492](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/492#issuecomment-6907598594). The code that handles the answer, until [issue #437](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/437) |

snippet.text: - A time limit and an output limit. The result is the exit code or the signal that ended the probe, the bounded output, whether it was cut, and whether the run timed out. bubblewrap reports a child a signal ended as exit 128+n, so the runner inside the sandbox records how the probe ended on a pipe of its own, and a probe with no such record reads as ended with no record of how. Node reports a child that a signal it cannot name killed, such as Linux's real-time signals, as exit 0, so the runner records exit 0 only when the probe's own exit handler, which no signal runs, reported 0 to it; any other exit 0 reads as ended with no record of how, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-17 that [the decision](decisions/2026-11-17-exit-0-needs-the-probes-own-report.md) records. Processes end by recorded pid, never by group.

snippet.text: Problem: the ruling of 2026-11-16 made Node's report of the probe's ending, `{ code, signal }`, the one authority for how a probe ended. Node reports a child that a signal it cannot name killed as exit 0 with no signal. On Linux that covers the real-time signals, 34 to 64. Example: Codex's seventh adversarial review of pull request #532 found that a probe that runs `process.kill(process.pid, 34)` read as exit 0, a passing, conclusive probe, so code under test could pass an attack by ending its own probe.

snippet.text: A run whose level sets `probe` carries `probe` in the lens task's input: the prober's route, thinking, instructions and `ProbingEnvironment`, the host's `WriterTrust`, the base's `trust.writers` and the time limit. Its conversation in `children` is the planner's, configured with the read tools, `report_finding` and `record_plan`, and a `LensPolicy` whose `role` is `planner`. When the planner finishes, the task reads the plan from its `ProbingDocument`, reminds a planner that recorded none once under the request ID `lens:<key>:plan`, and in one commit creates the prober's conversation under `<key>/prober` in `children` and `attempts`, with a copy of the plan. The prober runs on its own route with failover, as a lens does, from the input `renderPlan` writes; a prober that leaves attacks unanswered is reminded once under `lens:<key>/prober:answer`. An attack with a probe that failed is answered only when the prober reported a finding on one of its failed probes, which `report_finding` records in the `ProbingDocument`'s `answered`, or closed every one of them; any other attack, by a conclusive probe or a skip. `skip_attack` closes a probe when it names one: the probe must have run in the prober's conversation, probed that attack and failed, and its reason goes in the `ProbingDocument`'s `closed`, by probe ID. The lens's record ends its probing note with each closed probe and its reason, escaped with `visibleText`. `closed` is optional, so the document keeps version 3: a build without it ignores the field and reads the attack as unanswered, which ends the lens rather than passing it. `answered` is kept apart from `findings`, which holds only the first probe each finding rested on, since two attacks that fail on one defect report one finding ID; [issue #545](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/545) would keep every one. trigger.snippet: A run whose level sets `probe` carries `probe` in the lens task's input: the prober's route, thinking, instructions and `ProbingEnvironment`, the host's `WriterTrust`, the base's `trust.writers` and the time limit. Its conversation in `children` is the planner's, configured with the read tools, `report_finding` and `record_plan`, and a `LensPolicy` whose `role` is `planner`. When the planner finishes, the task reads the plan from its `ProbingDocument`, reminds a planner that recorded none once under the request ID `lens:<key>:plan`, and in one commit creates the prober's conversation under `<key>/prober` in `children` and `attempts`, with a copy of the plan. The prober runs on its own route with failover, as a lens does, from the input `renderPlan` writes; a prober that leaves attacks unanswered is reminded once under `lens:<key>/prober:answer`. An attack with a probe that failed is answered only when the prober reported a finding on one of its failed probes, which `report_finding` records in the `ProbingDocument`'s `answered`, or closed every one of them; any other attack, by a conclusive probe or a skip. `skip_attack` closes a probe when it names one: the probe must have run in the prober's conversation, probed that attack and failed, and its reason goes in the `ProbingDocument`'s `closed`, by probe ID. The lens's record ends its probing note with each closed probe and its reason, escaped with `visibleText`. `closed` is optional, so the document keeps version 3: a build without it ignores the field and reads the attack as unanswered, which ends the lens rather than passing it. `answered` is kept apart from `findings`, which holds only the first probe each finding rested on, since two attacks that fail on one defect report one finding ID; [issue #545](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/545) would keep every one. Version 3 of the document reads the attacks an older one answered from its `findings`. The outcome's `probing` holds the prober's conversation and model, the plan's size, the probes and their time, the skips and the attacks left unanswered, which end the lens. Version 6 of the lens task added these fields.
